# =============================================================================
# BPO Adriene — backend (FastAPI app) pinned dependency set
#
#   pip install -r backend/requirements-lock.txt
#
# Generated by resolving backend/requirements.txt for CPython 3.12 (the version
# the Dockerfile ships) with:
#   pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --python-version 3.12 \
#       --only-binary=:all: --report r.json -r backend/requirements.txt
#
# PINNED: the direct dependencies. Their transitive requirements are left to
# the resolver on purpose — see the torch note below, which is the reason a
# full freeze cannot be used here.
#
# NOT RUNNABLE ON PYTHON 3.13: kokoro 0.9.4 declares Requires-Python
# >=3.10,<3.13. Use 3.12 (as the Dockerfile does) for this file. The root
# requirements-lock.txt has no such cap and installs fine on 3.13.
# =============================================================================

cryptography==50.0.2
fastapi==0.162.0
uvicorn[standard]==0.54.0
python-multipart==0.0.33
sqlmodel==0.0.48
pytest==9.2.0

# Windows-only; the QA runner uses it for per-turn audio. Not installed
# elsewhere, so it is not pinned to a version.
pyttsx3>=2.99 ; sys_platform == 'win32'

# Local neural TTS (Kokoro-82M, 20 US-English voices).
kokoro==0.9.4

# --- deliberately NOT pinned here: torch ------------------------------------
# kokoro depends on torch, whose default linux wheel pulls ~2 GB of CUDA
# libraries (nvidia-cublas, nvidia-cudnn, ...). The Dockerfile installs the
# CPU-only build BEFORE this file so the CUDA stack is never selected:
#
#   RUN pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
#   RUN pip install -r backend/requirements-lock.txt
#
# Pinning torch here would re-introduce the CUDA build, so the torch version is
# owned by the Dockerfile's index URL instead. Resolved here it would be 2.15.0.
